title: Massachusetts follow-up periods after an oral controlled-substance prescription
rule_summary: Under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 20(c) a practitioner who prescribes a controlled substance by oral prescription shall cause an ELECTRONIC prescription to be delivered to the dispensing pharmacy WITHIN 2 DAYS; if the practitioner has received an electronic-prescribing exception from the commissioner under s. 23(h), the practitioner shall instead cause a WRITTEN prescription to be delivered within not more than 7 DAYS, or the shorter period required by federal law, postmarked within that period. The follow-up prescription must indicate that it documents an oral prescription, and the pharmacy attaches it to the oral prescription it reduced to writing. Under 105 CMR 721.070(B) a practitioner issuing an oral prescription for a controlled substance in SCHEDULES II THROUGH V under a 105 CMR 721.070(A) ePrescribing exception shall cause a written or electronic prescription to be delivered within not more than SEVEN BUSINESS DAYS, or the shorter period required by federal law. The s. 20(c) requirements do not apply to controlled substances in Schedule VI.
exam_relevance: Tests whether the candidate separates the 2-day electronic default, the 7-day written exception route, and the 7-business-day regulatory period instead of applying a single seven-day figure.

numeric_facts.fact: Practitioner electronic follow-up after an oral controlled-substance prescription
numeric_facts.conditions: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 20(c) default where the practitioner holds no s. 23(h) exception

numeric_facts.fact: Practitioner written follow-up where the practitioner holds a s. 23(h) exception
numeric_facts.conditions: Or the shorter period required by federal law; the writing must be postmarked within the period

numeric_facts.fact: Practitioner follow-up for an oral Schedule II-V prescription issued under a 105 CMR 721.070(A) exception
numeric_facts.conditions: Or the shorter period required by federal law

exceptions: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 20(c) does not apply to controlled substances in Schedule VI, although the immediate reduction to writing and the remaining validity duties still apply.
A shorter federal period controls where federal law requires one, such as the 7-day emergency oral Schedule II follow-up under 21 CFR 1306.11(d)(4).
common_confusions: Quoting a single seven-day figure for every Massachusetts oral controlled-substance follow-up and missing the 2-day electronic default.
Treating the 105 CMR 721.070(B) seven BUSINESS days as the same measure as the statutory seven days.
Reading the follow-up period as a deadline for the pharmacist rather than for the prescribing practitioner.
verification_notes: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 20 and s. 23 read verbatim on malegislature.gov, and 105 CMR 721.070(B) read verbatim in the current official publication dated 9/27/24, both on 2026-09-04 during Study Guide REPAIR-V3.
